task_description: Build a Claude tool-using agent with two overlapping search tools (`search_docs` and `search_kb`) and route user queries to the right one.
failure_reason: Tool descriptions overlapped and described WHAT each tool does without distinguishing WHEN to use one vs. the other, so Claude consistently picked the wrong tool.
error_message: (no API error) — agent silently selected the unintended tool; downstream answers cited the wrong corpus. Symptom matches Anthropic's 'Claude calls tool A when you wanted tool B' troubleshooting row.
what_was_tried: Iterating on the user-facing prompt to nudge Claude toward the right tool.
lesson: Tool selection is driven primarily by tool name + description, not by the user prompt. Differentiate tools by WHEN to use them, not only WHAT they do.
suggested_approach: Sharpen each tool description to specify its trigger conditions; add `input_examples`; consider `tool_choice` if you can hardcode routing for known intents.

task_description: Loop tool calls back into Claude after running them, but place a text message before the tool_result blocks in the user turn.
failure_reason: The Messages API requires every `tool_use` block in an assistant turn to be answered by a `tool_result` block in the next user turn, and the tool_result blocks must come before any text in that turn.
error_message: tool_use ids were found without tool_result blocks immediately after
what_was_tried: Building the next user turn as `[{type:'text', text:'Here are the results'}, {type:'tool_result', ...}]`.
lesson: Anthropic enforces strict ordering: one tool_result per tool_use, and tool_results must be the FIRST content blocks in the user turn.
suggested_approach: Construct the user turn as `[tool_result, tool_result, ..., (optional text)]` and emit one tool_result for every tool_use id from the assistant's previous response.

task_description: Enable Claude `strict: true` tool use on a schema that uses a regex `pattern` to validate an ID format.
failure_reason: Anthropic strict mode supports only a subset of JSON Schema; the `pattern` keyword is not in the supported subset.
error_message: Input schema is not compatible with strict mode: string patterns are not supported
what_was_tried: Copying a schema directly from a Pydantic model that used `Field(pattern=...)`.
lesson: Strict mode trades schema expressiveness for guarantees; not every JSON Schema feature works.
suggested_approach: Drop the `pattern` keyword and validate format in your tool implementation, or remove `strict: true` for that tool.

task_description: Enable Anthropic `tool_search` for a 200-tool catalog and mark every tool with `defer_loading: true` to save context.
failure_reason: At least one tool must be immediately loaded; the tool_search tool itself must never have defer_loading: true, and you cannot defer all tools.
error_message: All tools have defer_loading: true
what_was_tried: Setting defer_loading on every tool in the catalog assuming the model would request them on demand.
lesson: The model needs at least one tool visible to know what's available — typically tool_search itself.
suggested_approach: Leave `tool_search` always loaded (no defer_loading) and defer the long tail; let Claude pull in additional tools when they are relevant.

task_description: Compare serialized tool inputs across runs to detect agent drift after upgrading to Claude Opus 4.6.
failure_reason: Unicode and forward-slash escaping in serialized tool inputs differs between Claude model versions, so byte-equal string comparison fails even when the parsed objects are identical.
error_message: Tool input string differs between runs (illustrative): `"path": "\/api\/v1"` vs `"path": "/api/v1"`
what_was_tried: Snapshot-testing the JSON string of `tool_use.input` against a stored fixture.
lesson: Different model versions can serialize the same logical JSON differently; raw string equality is not a stable contract.
suggested_approach: Always parse with `json.loads()` / `JSON.parse()` and compare the resulting object structures rather than raw strings.

task_description: Send a user request that requires three independent web lookups and expect Claude to issue them in parallel.
failure_reason: The conversation alternated user/assistant after each tool call, so Claude never saw multiple tool_results arriving together and learned to call tools sequentially.
error_message: (no exception) — total latency was ~3x what parallel calls would yield.
tools_attempted: Claude Messages API parallel tool use
what_was_tried: Returning each tool_result in its own user message before sending the next request.
lesson: Parallel tool use depends on the message format: multiple tool_result blocks must be returned in ONE user message.
suggested_approach: Batch tool executions and return all results in a single user turn as `[tool_result, tool_result, tool_result]`.

task_description: Define an OpenAI function tool with `strict: true` and an optional `notes` field, leaving it out of the `required` array.
failure_reason: OpenAI strict mode requires every property under `properties` to appear in `required`; optionality is expressed via a nullable union, not omission.
error_message: Invalid schema for function 'X': In context=(), 'required' is required to be supplied and to be an array including every key in properties.
what_was_tried: Marking only truly mandatory fields as required, as in standard JSON Schema.
lesson: OpenAI strict mode reinterprets JSON Schema: every property must be required; nullability replaces optionality.
suggested_approach: Mark every property as required and use `"type": ["string", "null"]` for optional fields. Also set `additionalProperties: false` on every object.

task_description: Use OpenAI Structured Outputs response_format with a JSON Schema that omits `additionalProperties: false`.
failure_reason: Structured Outputs strict validation requires `additionalProperties: false` on every object; without it the request is rejected.
error_message: Invalid schema for response_format 'X': 'additionalProperties' is required to be supplied and to be false.
what_was_tried: Writing a JSON Schema by hand without the additionalProperties constraint.
lesson: Strict outputs require explicitly closing every object schema.
suggested_approach: Use Pydantic/zod with the SDK helper, which sets `additionalProperties: false` automatically; or add it yourself to every nested object.

task_description: Call OpenAI Structured Outputs with a deeply nested schema that uses `anyOf` at the root.
failure_reason: Root objects cannot be the `anyOf` type under Structured Outputs.
error_message: Invalid schema: root cannot be of type 'anyOf'. (illustrative paraphrase of Azure/OpenAI restriction)
what_was_tried: Defining the response shape as a discriminated union at the top level.
lesson: Some JSON Schema features are excluded from Structured Outputs to keep validation tractable.
suggested_approach: Wrap the union in an outer object with a single `result: anyOf[...]` field, or move the discrimination into a `kind` enum.

task_description: Stream a Structured Outputs response and validate against the schema as deltas arrive.
failure_reason: Strict-schema validation only happens on the complete response, so partial parses can produce schema-invalid intermediate fragments.
error_message: (client-side) Pydantic validation fails on a partial JSON object during streaming.
what_was_tried: Validating each delta with `MyModel.model_validate(json.loads(buffer))`.
lesson: Strict validation is a guarantee about the final message, not about the streaming bytes.
suggested_approach: Buffer the stream and validate once on completion, or use OpenAI's built-in `parse` helpers that handle partials safely.

task_description: Execute parallel function calls in Azure OpenAI alongside Structured Outputs.
failure_reason: Azure OpenAI Structured Outputs is not supported with parallel function calls or with the Assistants API.
error_message: There was an issue with your request. Please check your inputs and try again. (400; documented incompatibility)
what_was_tried: Setting `parallel_tool_calls=true` and a `response_format` schema in the same request.
lesson: Cloud-hosted variants can have stricter feature interaction matrices than the upstream provider.
suggested_approach: Disable parallel tool calls when using Structured Outputs on Azure, or move the structured step to a separate API call after tools resolve.

task_description: Connect an MCP-enabled coding agent to a third-party MCP server installed from a community registry.
failure_reason: Tool poisoning: malicious instructions were embedded in tool descriptions/metadata returned by the MCP server, hijacking the agent into exfiltrating local files.
error_message: (no error from agent) — agent silently followed instructions hidden in tool metadata; outbound HTTP request to attacker domain observed in network logs.
what_was_tried: Trusting the server description and tool list as data; not displaying full descriptions to the user before invocation.
lesson: MCP tool descriptions are untrusted input — they enter the model context with authority similar to system instructions.
suggested_approach: Pin and review server versions, surface full tool descriptions in approval UIs, sandbox MCP servers, and add static metadata scanners for prompt-injection patterns.

task_description: Have an LLM agent fetch a webpage and summarize it for an internal Slack channel.
failure_reason: Indirect prompt injection: the page contained hidden instructions (e.g., HTML comments or low-contrast text) telling the agent to post different content or call a destructive tool.
error_message: (no error) — agent followed instructions from the document instead of the user's original ask.
what_was_tried: Treating retrieved document text as trusted input alongside the user message.
lesson: Any text from the open web that ends up in the model's context can carry instructions. This is OWASP LLM01:2025.
suggested_approach: Tag retrieved content as untrusted, separate it visually in the prompt, restrict the agent's tool surface when handling external content, and add output filters for sensitive actions.

task_description: Give a customer-service agent broad write access to the CRM so it can 'help with anything'.
failure_reason: Excessive Agency (OWASP LLM06:2025): the agent had more capabilities than its task required, so a single prompt-injection caused mass record deletion.
error_message: (audit log) — `crm.delete_account` invoked from agent with no user-confirmation step.
tools_attempted: custom tool wrappers around CRM API
what_was_tried: Giving one tool full CRUD access for simplicity.
lesson: An LLM agent's blast radius equals the union of its tools' capabilities. Keep that surface as small as possible.
suggested_approach: Apply least-privilege to tools, split read vs write into separate agents, and require human approval for irreversible actions.

task_description: Build a chatbot whose system prompt contains an embedded admin password used by the backend tool.
failure_reason: System prompt leakage (OWASP LLM07:2025): users coaxed the model into reproducing the system prompt, exposing the secret.
error_message: (model output) — verbatim disclosure of system instructions including credentials.
what_was_tried: Treating the system prompt as private storage for secrets.
lesson: System prompts must be assumed extractable. They are configuration, not a vault.
suggested_approach: Fetch secrets server-side at tool execution time; never embed credentials, internal URLs, or PII in prompts.

task_description: Enrich 100k records with GPT-4o by firing requests in an asyncio.gather loop with no concurrency cap.
failure_reason: The caller exceeded the per-org TPM/RPM ceiling and did not implement backoff, causing repeated 429s.
error_message: Rate limit reached for gpt-4o in organization org-XXXX on tokens per min. Limit: 30000/min. Current: 30240/min. (illustrative format from OpenAI docs)
what_was_tried: No concurrency cap, no retry policy.
lesson: Rate limits are per-organization, enforced over short windows; bursts trigger 429 even with a paid plan.
suggested_approach: Add exponential backoff with jitter (per the OpenAI Cookbook), cap concurrency, or move bulk work to the Batch API.

task_description: Run a paid OpenAI account but receive 429 with type `insufficient_quota`.
failure_reason: 429 with `insufficient_quota` is a billing/quota error, not throttling; the org has used its monthly budget or has no positive credit balance.
error_message: Error code: 429 - {'error': {'message': 'You exceeded your current quota, please check your plan and billing details.', 'type': 'insufficient_quota', 'code': 'insufficient_quota'}}
what_was_tried: Adding exponential backoff, hoping the limiter would clear.
lesson: A 429 with `insufficient_quota` will never clear via retry; it requires billing action.
suggested_approach: Inspect the error `type` before retrying; on `insufficient_quota`, alert ops and stop sending traffic.

task_description: Ramp Anthropic Claude API traffic from 0 to 10,000 RPM in seconds for a launch.
failure_reason: Anthropic enforces acceleration limits; sharp traffic increases trigger 429s even when within steady-state quotas.
error_message: 429 — In rare cases, if your organization has a sharp increase in usage, you might see 429 errors due to acceleration limits on the API.
what_was_tried: Going from cold to peak load instantly during a marketing event.
lesson: Rate limits include rate-of-change limits, not just absolute ceilings.
suggested_approach: Pre-warm traffic gradually, maintain consistent usage patterns, and request a tier increase ahead of known spikes.

task_description: Call Anthropic Messages API during a high-traffic period and receive HTTP 529.
failure_reason: 529 `overloaded_error` indicates the API is temporarily overloaded across all users; it is not a per-account quota error.
error_message: 529 - overloaded_error: The API is temporarily overloaded.
what_was_tried: Treating 529 as a hard failure and surfacing an error to users.
lesson: 529 is transient. Retry with backoff before alarming users.
suggested_approach: Retry with exponential backoff and jitter; check status.claude.com to distinguish provider-side incidents from client-side problems.

task_description: Invoke Anthropic Claude Sonnet 3.5 via Amazon Bedrock with a single high-RPS workload in us-east-1.
failure_reason: Bedrock on-demand throttles per region from a shared capacity pool; you can hit ThrottlingException even within your own quotas if the regional pool is hot.
error_message: An error occurred (ThrottlingException) when calling the InvokeModel operation: Too many requests, please wait before trying again.
what_was_tried: Pinning to a single region with no cross-region inference profile.
lesson: On-demand Bedrock capacity is shared; single-region designs are fragile under spikes.
suggested_approach: Use cross-region inference profiles (e.g., `us.anthropic.claude-3-5-sonnet-...`), implement retries with jittered backoff, and consider Provisioned Throughput for predictable load.

task_description: Send long-context summarization jobs to Bedrock without limiting `max_tokens`.
failure_reason: Bedrock token-based throttling counts input + output + reserved `max_tokens` toward TPM, so leaving `max_tokens` huge consumes budget per request even when output is short.
error_message: An error occurred (ThrottlingException) when calling the InvokeModel operation: Too many tokens, please wait before trying again.
what_was_tried: Setting `max_tokens=4096` on every call regardless of the actual expected output size.
lesson: `max_tokens` reserves quota; right-sizing it is a primary throughput optimization on Bedrock.
suggested_approach: Set `max_tokens` to a tight per-call estimate, use streaming with early stop, and monitor `InputTokenCount`/`OutputTokenCount` in CloudWatch.

task_description: Use a brand-new AWS account to call Bedrock and discover models that should be available return ServiceQuotaExceededException.
failure_reason: New AWS accounts often start with quotas at very low or zero levels for Bedrock as a fraud-prevention measure.
error_message: Your request exceeds the service quota for your account. (May report 0 RPM/TPM on a new account.)
what_was_tried: Assuming default quotas matched documented public defaults.
lesson: Defaults documented on the page are upper bounds; new accounts get less.
suggested_approach: Check Service Quotas console early, file an increase request via AWS Support before launch, and verify per-region availability.

task_description: Stuff top-50 retrieved chunks into a Claude prompt for a long RAG answer.
failure_reason: The combined retrieval payload pushed the request past the model's context window, causing truncation of recent messages or a 413 request_too_large.
error_message: 413 request_too_large — Request exceeds the maximum allowed size.
what_was_tried: Increasing `top_k` to improve recall without measuring token cost.
lesson: More chunks doesn't mean better answers; it dilutes signal and risks 413s.
suggested_approach: Cap `top_k`, add a reranker, and measure prompt token count before sending; consider summarization or hierarchical retrieval.

task_description: Place the most important context (e.g., the user's question or schema) in the middle of a 100k-token prompt.
failure_reason: LLMs exhibit 'lost in the middle' behavior: information at the very beginning or end of long contexts is recalled more reliably than information in the middle.
error_message: (no API error) — model ignored or misused mid-context information; answers drifted from the schema.
what_was_tried: Inserting RAG chunks in retrieval-score order, leaving the user question buried.
lesson: Position matters in long prompts; LLMs over-attend to head and tail.
suggested_approach: Place critical instructions and the user query at the start AND the end; for RAG, rerank to push the most relevant chunks to the edges.
source_citations: https://arxiv.org/abs/2307.03172 (Liu et al., 'Lost in the Middle: How Language Models Use Long Contexts', 2023)

task_description: Set `max_tokens` to a very large value and rely on a synchronous (non-streaming) Anthropic call for a multi-minute generation.
failure_reason: Idle TCP connections were dropped by intermediate networks before the response completed, producing apparent timeouts.
error_message: Connection reset / timeout while waiting for response (illustrative; depends on network).
what_was_tried: Long blocking call with `max_tokens=8192` over an unreliable network.
lesson: Some networks drop idle connections after seconds; long single-shot calls are fragile.
suggested_approach: Use the streaming Messages API or the Message Batches API for long-running requests, and enable TCP keep-alive at the socket layer.

task_description: Continue an Anthropic conversation after a tool call but get an empty assistant response (~2-3 tokens, no content).
failure_reason: Claude can interpret the assistant turn as already complete after tool results — especially if the developer keeps adding empty text blocks or re-sends Claude's own completed reply.
error_message: (stop_reason: end_turn, content: []) — Claude returned no content despite a normal stop_reason.
what_was_tried: Adding a placeholder text block immediately after each tool_result.
lesson: Sentinel patterns Claude has seen during training (always-text-after-tool-results) can teach it to end its turn instead of continuing.
suggested_approach: Don't append text to user turns when only tool_results are needed; resend just the tool_result and let Claude continue.

task_description: Count tokens for a prompt by reusing a `tiktoken` encoder built for `gpt-3.5-turbo` against `gpt-4o`.
failure_reason: Different model families use different tokenizers (e.g., cl100k_base vs o200k_base); reusing the wrong encoder under-counts tokens.
error_message: openai.BadRequestError: This model's maximum context length is 128000 tokens; however your messages resulted in N tokens.
what_was_tried: Hard-coding `tiktoken.get_encoding('cl100k_base')` for all models.
lesson: Token counting is model-specific. Always look up the correct encoding per model.
suggested_approach: Use `tiktoken.encoding_for_model(model_name)`; for non-OpenAI models, use the provider's official token counter (e.g., Anthropic's token-counting API).

task_description: Build a vector RAG over policy docs; the agent confidently answers but cites the wrong policy.
failure_reason: Retrieval hallucination: the retriever returned chunks with shared keywords but unrelated meaning, and the LLM synthesized a plausible-sounding answer from irrelevant context.
error_message: (no exception) — high cosine similarity on the wrong chunks; answer is fluent but factually wrong.
what_was_tried: Trusting `similarity_top_k=3` without inspection or a reranker.
lesson: Vector similarity can match keywords without matching meaning.
suggested_approach: Add a cross-encoder reranker (e.g., CohereRerank or sentence-transformers); raise `similarity_top_k` and let the reranker prune; combine with BM25 hybrid search.

task_description: Chunk PDFs at a fixed 256-token size with no overlap and ingest into a vector store.
failure_reason: Critical context (e.g., a definition + the table that depends on it) was split across chunks, so no single retrieved chunk had enough information to answer.
error_message: (no exception) — partial answers; the right facts exist in the corpus but never appear together.
what_was_tried: Picking a small chunk size to maximize precision.
lesson: Chunking determines what's retrievable. Boundaries that cut definitions from their use sites are silent killers.
suggested_approach: Increase chunk size (e.g., 1024 tokens) with 10-20% overlap; prefer SentenceSplitter or HierarchicalNodeParser; use SentenceWindowNodeParser to retrieve a sentence but synthesize with neighbors.

task_description: Re-ingest updated documents into the existing vector index by appending new vectors.
failure_reason: Index fragmentation: stale and updated versions of the same document coexisted in the index, so retrieval returned contradictory chunks.
error_message: (no exception) — different answers across runs; contradictory information in retrieved chunks.
what_was_tried: Appending re-extracted chunks without dedup or doc_id tracking.
lesson: Without document-level identity, an index becomes a junk drawer.
suggested_approach: Track `doc_id` and use `index.refresh_ref_docs()` (LlamaIndex) or equivalent; keep a docstore for dedup; add metadata timestamps and filter on recency.

task_description: Upgrade the embedding model from `text-embedding-ada-002` to `text-embedding-3-large` without re-embedding the index.
failure_reason: Config drift / embedding mismatch: query and document embeddings now live in different vector spaces, collapsing similarity scores.
error_message: (no exception) — sudden, uniform drop in retrieval quality after a code change; similarity scores abnormally low across all queries.
what_was_tried: Swapping the embed_model in code only.
lesson: You cannot mix embeddings from different models in one index.
suggested_approach: Pin the embedding model alongside the index, log it in metadata, and rebuild the entire index whenever it changes.

task_description: Index legal contracts using a general-purpose embedding model and watch keyword search outperform vector search on user queries.
failure_reason: Embedding model mismatch for the domain: jargon and synonyms specific to legal text are poorly represented by general-purpose embeddings.
error_message: (no exception) — vector recall < BM25 recall on a labeled eval set.
what_was_tried: Defaulting to a generic embedding model without evaluating recall.
lesson: Embedding choice is a domain decision, not a default.
suggested_approach: Use a domain-adapted embedding model, fine-tune one on synthetic QA from your corpus, and add hybrid (vector + BM25) retrieval as a safety net.

task_description: Ask 'What did Q3 revenue look like?' and get an answer pulled from the previous year's earnings deck.
failure_reason: No metadata filtering: the retriever searched across all years, and last year's deck shared keywords with this year's.
error_message: (no exception) — answer cites the wrong fiscal year.
what_was_tried: Storing only raw text without structured metadata for date/source/department.
lesson: Filterable metadata is the cheapest precision improvement in RAG.
suggested_approach: Add date, source, department, version fields at ingest; use MetadataFilters at query time; consider auto-retrieval where the LLM extracts filters from the query.

task_description: Users send 1-2 word queries to a RAG chatbot and get useless answers; rephrasing the same query produces dramatically better results.
failure_reason: Poor query understanding: short or jargon-mismatched queries produce embeddings that don't align with how the documents are written.
error_message: (no exception) — high variance in answer quality between near-equivalent queries.
what_was_tried: Embedding the raw user query directly.
lesson: The user's question is rarely a good search string by itself.
suggested_approach: Add a query-rewrite/expansion step (HyDE, sub-question decomposition, or LLM-based rephrasing) before retrieval; provide example queries in the UI.

task_description: Retrieve the right chunks but the LLM still answers from its training data, ignoring the provided context.
failure_reason: LLM synthesis failure: prompt didn't constrain the model to use only retrieved context, and a weaker synthesis model leaned on priors.
error_message: (no exception) — manually verified chunks contain the answer; model output contradicts them.
what_was_tried: Default QA prompt with no system instruction enforcing context-only answers.
lesson: Without explicit instructions and a strong synthesizer, the model treats context as suggestion rather than ground truth.
suggested_approach: Customize the QA prompt to require context-only answers, use a stronger synthesis model, switch to Refine response mode, and add a system prompt reinforcing groundedness.

task_description: Adopt a vector store with cosine similarity for a corpus of mixed short FAQ entries and long policy documents.
failure_reason: Embedding metric mismatch: long generic chunks dominated the similarity ranking, pushing truly relevant short snippets out of the top-k.
error_message: (no exception) — relevant docs appear at rank 7-15; top-3 are bland generic text.
what_was_tried: Using one chunking strategy and one similarity metric for very different document types.
lesson: Length normalization, metric choice, and chunk uniformity all interact with what 'similar' means.
suggested_approach: Normalize/trim long chunks; add a reranker that uses a different scoring function; evaluate top-k beyond top-1 on a labeled eval set.

task_description: Ship a RAG service to production where the same query returns different answers across days even though no documents changed.
failure_reason: Session and cache memory breaks: cache eviction, inconsistent session keys, or vector store partial reindex made the searchable corpus drift between requests.
error_message: (no exception) — replaying the same query yields different result sets at different times.
what_was_tried: Treating the index/cache as fully stateless.
lesson: RAG correctness depends on infrastructure consistency, not just retrieval logic.
suggested_approach: Define explicit session/user keys; separate long-term knowledge from short-lived scratch; log index versions; replay a smoke-test query suite after every deploy.

task_description: Diagnose a RAG bug reported as 'sometimes the answer is weird' with no logs.
failure_reason: Observability gap: no traces of retrieval, prompts, scores, or index versions, so the failure can't be reproduced or located.
error_message: (no exception) — bugs are 'flaky' but unreproducible.
what_was_tried: Reading user-facing transcripts only.
lesson: If you can't replay the bug from logs, you can't fix it.
suggested_approach: Capture per-request: query, retrieved nodes, similarity scores, index/snapshot id, final prompt, model output. Use callbacks/tracing (LlamaIndex callback_manager, LangSmith, OpenTelemetry).

task_description: Deploy a new version of a RAG service; some queries return obviously empty answers right after rollout.
failure_reason: Index lifecycle / deployment ordering: production traffic was routed to the new version before ingestion finished, so the served index was empty or partial.
error_message: (no exception) — vector store reports far fewer nodes than expected; rollback fixes it.
what_was_tried: Decoupling code deploys from index builds without an order/health gate.
lesson: An index is a versioned artifact; treat it like one.
suggested_approach: Track an index version/snapshot id in both ingestion and serving paths; add a post-deploy smoke test that fails fast if the index is empty or under a min size threshold.

task_description: Mix Hugging Face `xenova/all-mpnet-base-v2` (768-dim) embeddings with documents previously embedded by Llama3 (4096-dim).
failure_reason: Embedding length mismatch: vectors of different dimensions cannot share an index; the SDK rejects writes/queries.
error_message: Embedding length mismatch (from llamaindex/dist/Embeddings utils.js)
what_was_tried: Switching embedding models mid-project without rebuilding.
lesson: Embedding dimensionality is a hard contract, not a config knob.
suggested_approach: Decide on an embedding model up front, store the dim in metadata, and re-index from scratch on any change.

task_description: Run a LangGraph 1.0.x text-to-SQL agent that should stop after returning a query result.
failure_reason: Agent looped indefinitely until LangGraph's recursion limit triggered; stop conditions in the prompt were ignored.
error_message: Recursion limit of 20 reached without hitting a stop condition. You can increase the limit by setting the `recursion_limit` config key.
what_was_tried: Adding 'stop after returning the result' to the prompt and increasing recursion_limit.
lesson: Termination must be explicit in graph state, not just in the prompt; LLMs don't reliably honor 'stop' instructions when tools keep returning new content.
suggested_approach: Add an explicit terminal node, hash-based loop detection, max_execution_time, and structured tool outputs that signal completion.

task_description: Read a large file via a tool that returns a few very long lines (e.g., minified JSON).
failure_reason: LangChain DeepAgents eviction loop: the result exceeded `toolTokenLimitBeforeEvict`, was written to the FS, then `read_file` returned the same oversized result, evicting again — the agent looped.
error_message: (no exception) — same tool result repeatedly evicted and re-read; cost climbs without progress.
what_was_tried: Using default eviction settings against a file with very long lines.
lesson: Limits expressed in lines fail when content has no line breaks; eviction policies need char/token caps.
suggested_approach: Cap read_file output by character/token count, exempt read_file from eviction, or chunk reads.

task_description: Run a multi-agent CrewAI/AutoGen pipeline where every agent passes work to the next agent for help.
failure_reason: No agent had a clear termination condition, so handoffs cycled indefinitely until budget capped them.
error_message: (no exception) — agents pass control back and forth past max_turns; or hit `Agent stopped due to max iterations`.
what_was_tried: Relying on default max_turns and prompt-level 'done' wording.
lesson: Multi-agent systems require explicit termination conditions; without them, 'ask another agent' is the safest default move.
suggested_approach: Set framework-level max_turns/max_iterations; add programmatic `is_termination_msg` predicates; use loop/cycle detection by hashing recent messages.

task_description: Use a CrewAI Agent with a custom (non-OpenAI-tool-format) LLM endpoint and a WebSearchTool.
failure_reason: The agent emitted Thought→Action→Observation→Final Answer in text but never actually invoked the tool; it fabricated tool output.
error_message: (no exception) — agent trace shows tool 'use'; downstream system shows zero tool calls.
what_was_tried: Trusting the agent's verbose log as proof that the tool ran.
lesson: ReAct-style text traces are not evidence of execution; CrewAI's tool dispatch only runs when the model emits the framework's expected tool-calling format.
suggested_approach: Verify with provider-side logs/metrics; prefer native function-calling LLMs; add tool-execution counters as a smoke test.

task_description: Set max_iterations=15 on a LangChain AgentExecutor that needs ~25 reasoning steps.
failure_reason: The agent hit the iteration ceiling and returned no final answer; downstream callers retried, multiplying cost.
error_message: Agent stopped due to iteration limit or time limit.
what_was_tried: Using default max_iterations without measuring the typical step distribution.
lesson: Step budgets are a guardrail, not a guess; measure p90 iteration count before tuning.
suggested_approach: Set max_iterations and max_execution_time appropriately; use early_stopping_method='generate' so callers receive a best-effort answer; add return_intermediate_steps for debugging.

task_description: Let an agent self-iterate with no chain-of-thought summarization between turns.
failure_reason: Goal drift: with each turn the agent re-derived the goal from a growing context, gradually pursuing tangentially related work.
error_message: (no exception) — final answer addresses an objective the user never stated.
what_was_tried: Appending every step to context without re-anchoring the original task.
lesson: Long agent contexts dilute the original goal; re-anchoring is mandatory.
suggested_approach: Re-state the goal at each iteration; periodically summarize state; use a planner step that checks 'did this step move us toward the goal?'

task_description: Add an Anthropic `cache_control` breakpoint on the system prompt, expecting tool definitions to be cached too.
failure_reason: Cache hierarchy is tools → system → messages; placing the breakpoint on system caches system but re-processes tools every call.
error_message: (no exception) — usage shows 0 cache_read_input_tokens for tools; cost climbs.
what_was_tried: Putting the only breakpoint on the system message.
lesson: A breakpoint caches everything BEFORE it in the hierarchy; placement matters.
suggested_approach: Place the breakpoint on the LAST tool definition to cache tools+system together; add additional breakpoints for RAG context and conversation history.

task_description: Toggle `tool_choice` between 'auto' and 'any' across requests in a Claude conversation.
failure_reason: Changes to `tool_choice` invalidate the cache for the entire request, eliminating cache hit savings.
error_message: (no exception) — every request shows cache_creation_input_tokens > 0 and cache_read_input_tokens == 0.
what_was_tried: Dynamically setting tool_choice per turn for routing logic.
lesson: Variation in tool_choice (and image presence) breaks the cache.
suggested_approach: Keep tool_choice stable for cacheable prefixes, or place the cache_control breakpoint earlier than the variation point.

task_description: Serialize Claude tool_use input from a Swift/Go service before sending it back as part of the conversation.
failure_reason: Some languages randomize JSON object key order; Claude's prompt cache lookup is byte-sensitive, so unstable key ordering breaks cache hits.
error_message: (no exception) — cache_read_input_tokens flips between 0 and N across otherwise identical requests.
what_was_tried: Using the standard library's JSON encoder without ordered keys.
lesson: Cache keys are based on byte identity. Map iteration randomness silently kills cache hit rates.
suggested_approach: Force stable key ordering when re-serializing tool_use blocks; in Go use `json.Encoder` with sorted maps; in Swift use ordered dictionaries.

task_description: Use Anthropic prompt caching on a system prompt that's slightly under 1024 tokens.
failure_reason: Cache writes have a minimum cacheable length (1024 tokens for Sonnet, 4096 for Opus/Haiku 4.5); shorter prefixes are not cached.
error_message: (no exception) — cache_creation_input_tokens stays at 0 despite cache_control being set.
what_was_tried: Marking a small system prompt with cache_control and expecting savings.
lesson: Prompt caching only helps above per-model minimums.
suggested_approach: Bundle system + tools (or RAG context) under one breakpoint to cross the minimum; otherwise skip caching for short prefixes.

task_description: Production code pinned to `gpt-3.5-turbo-0613` keeps running until the shutdown date.
failure_reason: The model was retired per OpenAI's deprecation schedule; all calls returned 404 / model_not_found after sunset.
error_message: The model `gpt-3.5-turbo-0613` does not exist or you do not have access to it.
what_was_tried: Pinning to a snapshot model and ignoring deprecation emails.
lesson: Snapshot model strings have a finite lifetime. Track the deprecations page.
suggested_approach: Subscribe to the OpenAI deprecations page; abstract the model string into config; periodically run a CI check that the model is still listed as supported.

task_description: Migrate code from the OpenAI Assistants API to the Responses + Conversations APIs.
failure_reason: Direct port assumed feature parity, but Responses uses different state semantics (no `previous_response_id` while attached to a conversation), different file_search config (vector_store_ids), and different storage TTLs.
error_message: (varies) — file_search returns no results; conversation state isn't carried as expected.
what_was_tried: Mechanical search-and-replace from `assistants.create` to `responses.create`.
lesson: API replacements are designs, not renames; semantics shift.
suggested_approach: Read the official Assistants→Responses migration guide; treat the cutover as a design change with eval coverage, not a refactor.

task_description: Run an Azure OpenAI deployment on `gpt-4o` version 2024-05-13 past 31 March 2026.
failure_reason: Azure auto-upgraded the deployment to `gpt-5.1` 2025-11-13 on the Standard SKU; provisioned customers had to migrate manually and saw inference fail.
error_message: 410 Gone (post-retirement) — model no longer serves inference. (illustrative)
what_was_tried: Assuming Azure's deprecation timeline mirrored OpenAI's.
lesson: Azure has its own retirement schedule and SKU-specific behavior; provisioned deployments don't auto-upgrade.
suggested_approach: Programmatically check `lifecycleStatus` and per-SKU `deprecationDate` via the Models API; plan migrations on Azure's calendar.

task_description: Use `from langchain.chat_models import ChatOpenAI` after upgrading to LangChain 0.3.
failure_reason: LangChain 0.2+ moved provider integrations into split packages (`langchain-openai`, `langchain-anthropic`, etc.); the old import still works but emits deprecation warnings and may break.
error_message: LangChainDeprecationWarning: Importing ChatOpenAI from langchain.chat_models is deprecated; please use `from langchain_openai import ChatOpenAI` instead.
what_was_tried: Following older tutorials.
lesson: LangChain's package split is the largest source of stale tutorial breakage.
suggested_approach: Update imports to provider packages; pin compatible versions of langchain-core, langchain, and langchain-openai/anthropic.

task_description: Set ANTHROPIC_API_KEY in a Docker .env file but the container can't reach the API.
failure_reason: The key was loaded into the build image but not into the running container's process environment, or it had whitespace/quotes around it.
error_message: 401 authentication_error — invalid x-api-key.
what_was_tried: Trusting the .env file would propagate at runtime.
lesson: Build-time env != run-time env; quoting and trailing whitespace silently invalidate keys.
suggested_approach: Echo the key at startup (masked), use `docker run --env-file` correctly, and verify the key with a `models.list` call as a health check.

task_description: Run a script that uses `dotenv` to load OPENAI_API_KEY but a stale shell variable shadows it.
failure_reason: An exported environment variable in the parent shell took precedence over the .env file; the wrong key was used.
error_message: 401 — Incorrect API key provided.
what_was_tried: Adding `load_dotenv()` at the top of the script.
lesson: `dotenv` does not override existing environment variables by default.
suggested_approach: Use `load_dotenv(override=True)`, or `unset OPENAI_API_KEY` before running, or explicitly pass `api_key=...` to the client.

task_description: Use an LLM to summarize legal text and surface citations the user can click.
failure_reason: The model invented citations that look plausible (real-sounding case names + plausible reporters) but don't exist.
error_message: (no exception) — fabricated citation `Smith v. Jones, 234 F.3d 567 (9th Cir. 2019)` does not exist.
what_was_tried: Trusting the model to generate citations from training-data memory.
lesson: LLMs fluently hallucinate structured-looking artifacts. Format isn't evidence of provenance.
suggested_approach: Ground citations in retrieval results; require the model to quote and cite by document_id; verify every citation against the source corpus before display.

task_description: Reproduce the same LLM answer across runs for a regression test.
failure_reason: LLMs are non-deterministic; even at temperature 0, output can vary across infra/version updates.
error_message: (no exception) — snapshot tests flap.
what_was_tried: Asserting exact-match equality of model outputs.
lesson: LLMs cannot be made fully deterministic; eval needs to be semantic.
suggested_approach: Set temperature=0, fix the model snapshot, and use semantic assertions (LLM-as-judge, schema validation, embedding similarity) instead of byte equality.

task_description: Direct user input flows verbatim into an LLM agent that has shell-execution tools.
failure_reason: A user prompt-injected the agent into running `rm -rf` via the shell tool.
error_message: (audit log) — destructive shell command executed; OWASP LLM01.
what_was_tried: No guardrails between user prompt and tool execution.
lesson: Direct user → agent → shell pipelines are dangerous by default.
suggested_approach: Add a planner/critic separation, restrict shell allowlist, require human approval for destructive commands, and run in an ephemeral sandbox.
source_citations: https://genai.owasp.org/llm-top-10/ (LLM01:2025 Prompt Injection, LLM06:2025 Excessive Agency)

task_description: Expose an open chat endpoint with no per-user rate limit.
failure_reason: A bot iterated huge prompts to inflate token usage ('denial of wallet') causing a $15k/month spike.
error_message: (billing alert) — sustained token-usage spike from a single IP.
what_was_tried: Trusting frontend rate limits and authentication-only protection.
lesson: LLM endpoints are direct cost vectors; absent server-side limits, abuse becomes a billing event.
suggested_approach: Per-user/IP RPM and TPM caps, max input length, max_tokens cap, alerting on spend velocity, and CAPTCHAs for unauthenticated traffic.

task_description: Run an autonomous coding agent overnight that retries failures aggressively.
failure_reason: Retry storms on transient errors compounded with long-context billing, racking up thousands of dollars before morning.
error_message: (billing alert) — token usage 50x baseline.
what_was_tried: Treating transient errors with infinite retries.
lesson: Naive retry on a long-context LLM call multiplies cost by every failure.
suggested_approach: Cap retries (e.g., 3), use jittered backoff, set hard daily/weekly spend caps via the provider's usage-limits dashboard, and alert on rate of spend.

task_description: Send a 25 MB PNG to Claude vision for OCR.
failure_reason: Anthropic enforces request size limits; oversized images return 413.
error_message: 413 request_too_large — Request exceeds the maximum allowed size.
what_was_tried: Sending the original image without resizing or compression.
lesson: Provider limits for image/PDF size are real constraints, not soft suggestions.
suggested_approach: Resize and compress images client-side (e.g., max 1568px on the long edge), or chunk PDFs by page.

task_description: OCR a scanned PDF by sending each page as a JPEG to GPT-4o.
failure_reason: Image-detail defaulted to 'auto' which downsampled tiny text, producing nonsense OCR for fine print.
error_message: (no exception) — illegible characters; tables misaligned.
what_was_tried: Default image_detail and small images.
lesson: Image-detail directly controls the budget the model spends on a region; default is a tradeoff.
suggested_approach: Set `image_detail='high'` for OCR; supply higher-resolution crops; consider a dedicated OCR engine before the LLM.

task_description: Consume an Anthropic streamed Messages response and treat HTTP 200 as a guarantee of success.
failure_reason: Errors can occur mid-stream after the 200 status; standard try/except around the request misses them.
error_message: event: error\ndata: {"type":"error","error":{"type":"overloaded_error","message":"Overloaded"}}
what_was_tried: Wrapping only the initial connect call in error handling.
lesson: Streaming success is per-event, not per-response.
suggested_approach: Inspect every event for `type:error`, set timeouts on idle stream chunks, and have a clean retry path that resumes from the last assistant content.

task_description: Upsert 5M vectors into a Pinecone serverless index in a tight loop.
failure_reason: Burst writes exceeded per-pod or serverless ingestion limits; some upserts silently failed without backoff.
error_message: 429 Too Many Requests (during upsert).
what_was_tried: Single-thread tight loop with no batching.
lesson: Vector DBs have ingest limits too; assume rate limits exist.
suggested_approach: Batch upserts (e.g., 100 per call), use parallel workers within the documented limit, retry with backoff, and verify count after ingest.

task_description: Query a Qdrant collection using cosine distance on un-normalized vectors.
failure_reason: Cosine assumes magnitude is irrelevant, but un-normalized OpenAI embeddings can produce inconsistent ranking when collection settings expect normalized inputs.
error_message: (no exception) — top-k results don't match expectations on a known-good test set.
what_was_tried: Setting distance=Cosine without normalizing vectors.
lesson: Distance metric and vector preprocessing must match.
suggested_approach: Normalize embeddings before insert/query, or pick the matching distance (Dot for un-normalized, Cosine for normalized).

task_description: Build an LLM-as-judge eval that compares model output to a reference using a 1-5 scoring rubric.
failure_reason: The judge LLM exhibited known biases: position bias (preferring the first response), self-preference (preferring outputs similar to its own style), and length bias.
error_message: (eval drift) — judge scores correlate weakly with human labels.
what_was_tried: Naive A vs B comparison without bias mitigation.
lesson: LLM judges are reliable only with explicit bias controls.
suggested_approach: Randomize order, run both orders and average, control for length, calibrate against a small human-labeled set, and prefer rubric-based scoring with chain-of-thought.
source_citations: https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.05685 (Zheng et al., 'Judging LLM-as-a-Judge with MT-Bench and Chatbot Arena', 2023)

task_description: Submit a JSONL Batch API job to OpenAI for nightly enrichment with a tight 24h SLA.
failure_reason: The batch expired in `in_progress` after 24h without completing; per OpenAI's contract, expired batches are not refunded automatically.
error_message: (batch.status: expired) — completion_window: 24h elapsed without all requests finishing.
what_was_tried: Treating the 24-hour completion window as guaranteed.
lesson: Batch is best-effort within 24h; pipelines built on it must tolerate expiration.
suggested_approach: Architect the pipeline to retry expired batches by splitting them into smaller chunks; alert when in-progress > 12h; keep a synchronous fallback for time-sensitive rows.

task_description: Build the Batch API JSONL by `json.dumps`-ing a list, then writing it to disk.
failure_reason: JSONL requires one JSON object per line; emitting a single JSON array (or pretty-printed objects with embedded newlines) breaks the parser server-side.
error_message: error_file_id contains rows with code `invalid_json_line`.
what_was_tried: Using `json.dumps(list_of_objects, indent=4)`.
lesson: JSONL ≠ JSON; the line-delimited contract is strict.
suggested_approach: Write one compact JSON object per line, no indentation; validate locally with a JSONL linter before upload.

task_description: Submit Azure OpenAI Batch jobs back-to-back with input that fits within the documented enqueued-token limit.
failure_reason: Azure enforces internal queueing policies that can fail jobs with 'enqueued token limit surpassed' even when math says you're under quota; the limit doesn't reset immediately when you cancel.
error_message: `enqueued_token_limit_reached` (Azure-internal queueing throttle).
what_was_tried: Submitting many small batches in rapid succession.
lesson: Documented quotas are upper bounds; queueing has its own dynamics.
suggested_approach: Throttle batch submission frequency, monitor `cancelling_at`/`expired_at`, and stagger jobs with a backoff between submissions.

task_description: Fine-tune `gpt-3.5-turbo-0613` for a domain assistant after the deprecation cutoff.
failure_reason: Fine-tuning on legacy/deprecated base models is blocked after the announced training-cutoff date even if inference still works for a while.
error_message: The base model `gpt-3.5-turbo-0613` is no longer eligible for fine-tuning.
what_was_tried: Pinning to an older base model for stability.
lesson: Fine-tuning lifecycles trail base-model lifecycles; pin only with an exit plan.
suggested_approach: Re-train on a current base model (e.g., gpt-4o-mini) before the documented training cutoff; export your dataset and rebuild as a one-shot job.

task_description: Fine-tune a model on a JSONL dataset assembled from chat logs without a clear `system`/`user`/`assistant` schema.
failure_reason: Fine-tuning examples must match the chat completions message schema; malformed roles or missing assistant turns cause job failure.
error_message: `Invalid file format. Expected JSONL with messages array per line.`
what_was_tried: Direct upload of cleaned chat logs.
lesson: Fine-tuning has strict schema requirements that the validator enforces only at job creation.
suggested_approach: Run the OpenAI data-validation script (cookbook) before submitting; ensure each line has a `messages` array with valid roles and content.

task_description: Use `pgvector` with HNSW indexes and add 100k new vectors in production traffic.
failure_reason: HNSW index rebuilds on bulk insert can lock or degrade query latency; default `ef_construction` was too high for the write rate.
error_message: (no exception) — query p99 latency 10x baseline during bulk insert.
what_was_tried: Bulk insert with default HNSW parameters mid-day.
lesson: ANN index maintenance has runtime cost; defaults aren't tuned for your workload.
suggested_approach: Tune `ef_construction` and `m`; use IVFFlat for write-heavy workloads; perform bulk inserts off-peak; consider parallel index build.

task_description: Switch a Weaviate collection's vectorizer from `text2vec-openai` to `text2vec-cohere` without re-indexing.
failure_reason: The collection's stored vectors were produced by the old vectorizer; queries from the new vectorizer were in a different space.
error_message: (no exception) — recall collapses; nearest neighbors are essentially random.
what_was_tried: Updating the schema's vectorizer config in place.
lesson: Changing the vectorizer is equivalent to changing the embedding model; the index must be rebuilt.
suggested_approach: Reingest the data through the new vectorizer; if downtime is unacceptable, write to a parallel collection and cut over with traffic shadowing.

task_description: Run an LLM-powered service behind a corporate proxy that strips Server-Sent Events.
failure_reason: The proxy buffered or terminated long-lived streaming connections, so client never received SSE events.
error_message: (no exception) — request hangs and eventually times out.
what_was_tried: Streaming through default corporate egress.
lesson: SSE depends on long-lived connections that some proxies don't support.
suggested_approach: Bypass the proxy for LLM endpoints, use HTTP/2, or switch to non-streaming for that environment.

task_description: Use the `openai` Python SDK with `httpx` set to a 10-second total timeout for everything.
failure_reason: LLM responses regularly take >10s; a global short timeout aborts even healthy requests.
error_message: ReadTimeout: timed out (default httpx timeout exceeded).
what_was_tried: Inheriting a tight default timeout from another HTTP client.
lesson: LLM calls need timeouts measured in minutes, not seconds.
suggested_approach: Set per-request `timeout` (e.g., 60-300s read, longer for reasoning models), or use streaming with a shorter idle-event timeout.

task_description: Use `temperature=0.3` and `top_p=0.9` with an o-series reasoning model.
failure_reason: o-series reasoning models ignore most sampling parameters (temperature, top_p, presence_penalty, frequency_penalty); requests with them succeed but the params have no effect, leading to confusing eval results.
error_message: (no exception) — eval scores don't change when temperature is varied.
what_was_tried: Reusing existing chat-completion configs for reasoning models.
lesson: Reasoning models have a different parameter contract; sampling knobs are inert.
suggested_approach: Drop the unused params; tune `reasoning_effort` instead; budget for higher latency and output token usage.

task_description: Cap `max_completion_tokens` at 1024 on an o3 reasoning model expecting compact answers.
failure_reason: Reasoning tokens are billed and counted toward the output limit; a tight cap can exhaust the budget on internal reasoning before any visible answer is produced.
error_message: (stop_reason: length / max_output_tokens) — completion contains hidden reasoning tokens but no assistant content.
what_was_tried: Reusing the chat-completion convention of small max_tokens.
lesson: Reasoning models 'think' in tokens that count against the output budget; sizes need to be far larger than for non-reasoning models.
suggested_approach: Increase `max_completion_tokens` significantly; monitor `usage.reasoning_tokens`; pick a smaller `reasoning_effort` if compactness matters.

task_description: Use Anthropic extended thinking and pass back the assistant's `thinking` blocks alongside `tool_result` for the next turn.
failure_reason: Forgetting to pass thinking blocks back when continuing a tool-use turn breaks Claude's ability to maintain reasoning state and can invalidate prompt caching.
error_message: (no exception) — degraded answer quality and unexpected cache misses on Sonnet 4.5.
what_was_tried: Stripping `thinking` blocks from the assistant turn before resending.
lesson: Thinking blocks are part of the conversation contract during tool use; dropping them resets reasoning context.
suggested_approach: Pass thinking blocks back unchanged on subsequent turns when continuing tool use; rely on documented model-specific cache behavior.

task_description: Build a voice agent on `gpt-4o-realtime-preview-2024-10-01` and pin the model snapshot.
failure_reason: OpenAI deprecated this snapshot on 10 June 2025 and removed it 3 months later; pinned voice agents went dark.
error_message: 404 — model `gpt-4o-realtime-preview-2024-10-01` not found.
what_was_tried: Treating preview snapshots as long-lived endpoints.
lesson: Preview models have shorter lifecycles than GA models; assume aggressive deprecation.
suggested_approach: Track the deprecations page closely for preview models; abstract the model id; build a smoke test that tags failures clearly when the model id 404s.

task_description: Pass an LLM-generated SQL query directly into a database driver as a string.
failure_reason: The LLM produced an injection-style payload (e.g., `; DROP TABLE users;`); the unparameterized execution ran it.
error_message: (audit log) — destructive SQL executed; OWASP LLM05:2025 Improper Output Handling.
what_was_tried: Trusting LLM output as if it came from a parameterized query builder.
lesson: LLM output is untrusted user input; never inject it into shells, SQL, HTML, or templates without validation.
suggested_approach: Use parameterized queries only, route through an allowlist of operations, render output via a context-aware escaper, and require explicit confirmation for write operations.

task_description: Render LLM-generated Markdown directly into a web page that allows raw HTML.
failure_reason: The LLM emitted an `` payload obtained via prompt injection from a fetched document, leading to XSS.
error_message: (SOC alert) — XSS in rendered chatbot answer.
what_was_tried: Rendering Markdown without sanitization.
lesson: LLMs cheerfully reproduce HTML/JS payloads; output sanitization is mandatory.
suggested_approach: Sanitize with DOMPurify or equivalent; render Markdown in a strict mode that disables raw HTML; CSP nonce all inline scripts.

task_description: Adopt a community LangChain integration package without pinning its version.
failure_reason: Supply-chain attack: a malicious release replaced a downstream provider package, exfiltrating API keys via a postinstall hook.
error_message: (SCA alert) — unexpected outbound traffic from a CI runner during build.
what_was_tried: Using floating versions and trusting the registry.
lesson: LLM tooling has the same supply-chain risk as any package ecosystem; floats are unsafe.
suggested_approach: Pin exact versions, lock with `pip-compile`/`uv lock`/`npm shrinkwrap`, run an SCA scan, and use `--require-hashes` in CI.

task_description: Fine-tune a model on user-submitted feedback that includes adversarial prompts.
failure_reason: Data poisoning: malicious examples taught the model unsafe behaviors that surface only on specific triggers.
error_message: (eval drift) — model emits attacker-controlled output on specific phrases.
what_was_tried: Mixing arbitrary user data into training without filtering.
lesson: Training-data quality controls are part of the security boundary.
suggested_approach: Sanitize and review training data, run anomaly/PII detection, hold out a poisoning canary set, and audit fine-tuned models with a red-team evaluation.

task_description: Index a multi-tenant RAG system in a single vector collection with no per-tenant filter.
failure_reason: Cross-tenant retrieval leaked one tenant's documents into another's queries (OWASP LLM08:2025 Vector and Embedding Weaknesses).
error_message: (audit) — Customer A's chunk surfaced as context for Customer B's query.
what_was_tried: Single shared collection with no metadata-filtered queries.
lesson: Vector stores are not auth boundaries; tenant isolation is your job.
suggested_approach: Per-tenant namespaces or per-tenant filters enforced server-side; reject queries with no tenant filter; verify isolation in CI tests.

task_description: Implement a chat history store that appends every user/assistant turn forever.
failure_reason: Unbounded conversation history blew past the context window; later turns truncated the system prompt or critical earlier context.
error_message: (no exception) — agent forgets earlier instructions; quality degrades after ~50 turns.
what_was_tried: Sending the full transcript on every turn.
lesson: Conversation memory needs a strategy: summarization, sliding window, or RAG over history.
suggested_approach: Use a summarization buffer, drop old turns past a threshold, store full history out-of-context for retrieval, or use Anthropic's context editing/compaction features.

task_description: Run a LangGraph agent with checkpointing across processes using an in-memory SqliteSaver.
failure_reason: In-memory state was lost on process restart; resumed runs started from scratch.
error_message: (no exception) — checkpoint missing for thread_id after crash.
what_was_tried: Treating the in-memory checkpointer as durable.
lesson: `:memory:` SQLite is per-process; checkpoints need persistent storage to survive restarts.
suggested_approach: Use a file-backed SQLite, Postgres, or Redis checkpointer; verify persistence with a kill/restart test.

task_description: Embed 1M docs with `text-embedding-3-large` and store full 3072-dim vectors in Pinecone.
failure_reason: Storage and query cost scaled with dimensionality; latency and bill ballooned versus a 1536-dim model.
error_message: (billing/latency dashboard) — 2x cost and 1.5x latency with marginal quality gain.
what_was_tried: Defaulting to the largest embedding model.
lesson: Embedding dimensionality has cost/latency consequences across the stack.
suggested_approach: Use Matryoshka dimensions (e.g., truncate to 1024 or 512), or prefer text-embedding-3-small if quality on your eval is comparable.

task_description: Display LLM medical guidance to end users without disclaimers or human review.
failure_reason: Overreliance / misinformation (OWASP LLM09:2025): the model produced confident, plausible advice that was clinically wrong.
error_message: (incident) — user followed inaccurate dosage guidance.
what_was_tried: Treating LLM outputs as authoritative.
lesson: LLM fluency creates an illusion of authority; high-stakes domains require provenance + human review.
suggested_approach: Restrict topics, attach grounded citations, require human-in-the-loop for high-stakes answers, surface uncertainty, and add evals for harmful misinformation.

task_description: Pipe internal CRM data into an LLM prompt to summarize a customer history.
failure_reason: Sensitive PII (SSN, payment data) entered the model context; downstream logging captured the prompt verbatim, leaking it into log aggregation.
error_message: (SIEM alert) — PII detected in observability backend.
what_was_tried: Logging full prompts and responses for debugging.
lesson: Prompts and responses are now part of your data flow; redact like any other data path.
suggested_approach: Redact PII before logging, use field-level allowlists, encrypt at rest, and apply data-residency rules to model providers.

task_description: Deploy an autonomous agent into production without continuous monitoring or rollback plan.
failure_reason: Without ongoing measurement and management (NIST AI RMF: Measure, Manage), drift, regression, and emergent harms accumulated unnoticed.
error_message: (post-mortem) — agent quality regressed silently for weeks.
what_was_tried: One-time eval before launch, no production telemetry.
lesson: LLM systems require continuous evaluation in production, not just pre-launch.
suggested_approach: Adopt NIST AI RMF practices: continuous monitoring, drift detection, eval canaries, incident response, and human-review feedback loops.

task_description: Wrap every LLM call in a `tenacity` retry decorator with `retry=retry_if_exception_type(Exception)`.
failure_reason: The decorator retried non-retryable errors (auth, schema validation, content moderation) indefinitely, multiplying cost and obscuring the root cause.
error_message: (no exception) — retries hide a 401/400 that should fail fast.
what_was_tried: Catching all exceptions and retrying.
lesson: Retry policies must distinguish transient (429/5xx) from permanent (4xx) errors.
suggested_approach: Retry only on rate limits, 5xx, and timeouts; never retry on 400/401/403/404; respect `Retry-After` headers; cap attempts.

task_description: Define a tool with a JSON Schema parameter `enum` of 200 string values.
failure_reason: Very large enums hurt model accuracy and waste tokens; the model frequently generated values outside the enum or off by case.
error_message: (no exception) — invalid enum value emitted; downstream validation rejects it.
what_was_tried: Listing every possible value as an enum to constrain output.
lesson: Enums are best for small, semantically meaningful sets.
suggested_approach: Shrink the enum, group categories, or accept free-form strings + server-side fuzzy match. Use strict mode for true closed sets.

task_description: Define two tools with similar names: `get_user` and `get_user_profile`.
failure_reason: Tool name collision/ambiguity led the model to pick whichever appeared first or to use them interchangeably.
error_message: (no exception) — agent uses the wrong tool, returning incomplete data.
what_was_tried: Naming tools by the underlying API method.
lesson: Tool names are part of the prompt; ambiguity costs accuracy.
suggested_approach: Use distinctive, intent-oriented names (`get_user_basic` vs `get_user_full_profile`); ensure descriptions disambiguate with WHEN-to-use guidance.

task_description: Spawn 200 concurrent LLM requests with `asyncio.gather` against a 10 RPS rate limit.
failure_reason: No semaphore controlled concurrency; the burst hit rate limits, all requests retried with backoff, and effective throughput plummeted.
error_message: (no exception, observed) — total elapsed time longer than serial execution due to retry storm.
what_was_tried: `gather` with no concurrency cap, relying on SDK retries.
lesson: Concurrency without backpressure exceeds rate limits and triggers retries that destroy throughput.
suggested_approach: Use `asyncio.Semaphore`, a token-bucket limiter (e.g., `aiolimiter`), or a worker-pool with a request queue.

task_description: Enable Amazon Bedrock Guardrails on InvokeModel and forget to provide both `guardrailIdentifier` and `guardrailVersion`.
failure_reason: Bedrock requires both fields when guardrails are enabled, and content type must be application/json; missing either errors out.
error_message: ValidationException — guardrailVersion is required when guardrailIdentifier is provided.
what_was_tried: Wiring up the guardrail id but omitting the version.
lesson: Guardrail config is paired metadata; partial config is rejected.
suggested_approach: Always pass both `guardrailIdentifier` and `guardrailVersion`; treat `DRAFT` as a development-only value.

task_description: Pin a production image-generation pipeline to `dall-e-3`.
failure_reason: OpenAI scheduled `dall-e-2` and `dall-e-3` for shutdown on 12 May 2026 with `gpt-image-1` as replacement; pinned pipelines will fail post-sunset.
error_message: 404 — model `dall-e-3` no longer available (post-shutdown).
what_was_tried: Treating image-gen models as long-lived endpoints.
lesson: Image-gen migrations also change prompt behavior, output sizes, and moderation profiles — not just the model id.
suggested_approach: Migrate to `gpt-image-1` ahead of the shutdown; A/B test prompt outputs and downstream moderation; budget for retraining brand-review tooling.

task_description: Parse an LLM's response that should contain a JSON object embedded in markdown code fences.
failure_reason: Naive `json.loads()` on the full string failed because of code fences and stray prose; the model also occasionally emitted JSON5-style trailing commas.
error_message: json.decoder.JSONDecodeError: Expecting value / Extra data.
what_was_tried: Stripping just ```json fences, no other normalization.
lesson: Free-form generation produces near-JSON often, exact-JSON sometimes.
suggested_approach: Use Structured Outputs / strict tool use to guarantee schema; if not possible, parse with a tolerant library (e.g., `json5`, `dirtyjson`) and validate with Pydantic.

task_description: Ask an LLM 'when is the next Tuesday?' with no current-date context.
failure_reason: The model used its training-data 'today' as anchor and produced a date in the past or wrong week.
error_message: (no exception) — answer references a date months out of date.
what_was_tried: Trusting the model to know the current date.
lesson: LLMs don't have an internal clock; current-time context must be supplied.
suggested_approach: Inject `current_date` into the system prompt or as a tool; never rely on the model to know 'now'.

task_description: Use OpenAI `response_format=json_schema` AND function tools at the same time, expecting both to be enforced together.
failure_reason: `response_format` constrains the final assistant message after tools resolve; users expected it to also constrain intermediate tool arguments and got confused when behavior didn't match.
error_message: (no exception) — schema isn't applied where the developer expected.
what_was_tried: Setting both and assuming they composed.
lesson: Tool-call args use the tool's own JSON Schema; response_format only governs the final assistant content.
suggested_approach: Put per-tool schemas on the tool definitions (with `strict: true`); keep `response_format` for the final structured answer once tools have run.

task_description: Run a LangChain chain that expects two input variables but call `chain.invoke('hello')`.
failure_reason: LangChain expects a dict input matching the prompt's input variables; passing a string is a common mistake after migrating from LLMChain.
error_message: ValueError: Missing some input keys: {'name', 'age'}
what_was_tried: Passing positional/string input as in older versions.
lesson: LCEL invocation is dict-typed; the schema is enforced at runtime.
suggested_approach: Inspect `prompt.input_variables`; pass `chain.invoke({'name': 'Alice', 'age': 30})`.

task_description: Use `OutputParserException` retry logic in LangChain expecting it to recover from any parser failure.
failure_reason: The retry parser sends the malformed output back to the same LLM with the same prompt, which often produces the same bad output.
error_message: OutputParserException — failed to parse output.
what_was_tried: Trusting `OutputFixingParser` to fix any error.
lesson: Retries don't substitute for structural constraints.
suggested_approach: Switch to function calling / Structured Outputs / strict tool use; only fall back to OutputFixingParser for legacy chains.

task_description: Send EU customer prompts to OpenAI's US endpoint without enabling EU data residency.
failure_reason: Data residency violation: prompts containing EU PII transited US servers, breaching GDPR data-residency commitments.
error_message: (audit) — DPIA flag on transatlantic data flow.
what_was_tried: Defaulting to the global endpoint.
lesson: LLM endpoints have data-residency implications that must be reconciled with regulation.
suggested_approach: Use EU/region-specific deployments (Azure OpenAI region pinning, Anthropic data residency, Bedrock per-region endpoints); document data flow in a DPIA.

task_description: Debug a flaky agent with `print` statements scattered through tool wrappers.
failure_reason: Without structured tracing, reproducing a failure required re-running the agent and hoping it failed the same way.
error_message: (no exception) — failure can't be re-played; root cause unknown.
what_was_tried: Ad hoc logging.
lesson: Agent debugging needs trace-level observability: per-step inputs, tool calls, tokens, latency.
suggested_approach: Adopt OpenTelemetry, LangSmith, or Phoenix; capture span trees of agent runs; redact PII before storage.

task_description: Run Anthropic computer-use agent on a public webpage that turns out to contain hidden prompt-injection text.
failure_reason: Page-level prompt injection redirected the agent to perform unrelated actions including file uploads.
error_message: (no exception) — agent diverged from user intent after rendering injected content.
what_was_tried: Letting the agent operate on arbitrary pages.
lesson: Browser agents inherit the trust level of every page they view; that's effectively the open web.
suggested_approach: Restrict navigation to allowlisted domains, require user confirmation on irreversible actions, run inside a sandbox VM, and add output filters before destructive tool calls.

task_description: Treat 5xx errors from the OpenAI API as application bugs and page on-call.
failure_reason: The errors were a provider-side incident; on-call thrashed instead of waiting it out and switching to a fallback.
error_message: 500 — server_error: The server had an error while processing your request.
what_was_tried: Treating provider 5xx as our fault.
lesson: Cross-reference status pages before deep-debugging a 5xx.
suggested_approach: Add an automated check against `status.openai.com` / `status.anthropic.com`/`status.aws.amazon.com` in incident runbooks; configure fallback providers; set SLO budgets that exclude provider incidents.

task_description: Upgrade `langchain-core` independently of `langchain` and `langchain-openai`.
failure_reason: Version skew between the meta package and provider packages produced subtle import errors and behavioral differences.
error_message: ImportError / AttributeError on previously working chains after partial upgrade.
what_was_tried: Upgrading one package at a time.
lesson: The LangChain ecosystem has tight inter-package compatibility; partial upgrades break.
suggested_approach: Upgrade `langchain`, `langchain-core`, and provider packages together; pin compatible ranges; pre-test with `pip-compile`.

task_description: Use OpenAI Structured Outputs and assume the parsed object is always populated.
failure_reason: The model can issue a `refusal` instead of producing the schema; client code that didn't handle `refusal` got `None` and crashed.
error_message: (no exception from API) — `parsed` is None; `refusal` field is populated.
what_was_tried: Treating Structured Outputs as 'always returns the schema'.
lesson: Refusals are first-class; safety-relevant outputs are returned as a refusal field.
suggested_approach: Check `message.refusal` first; surface a graceful UX or escalate; do not parse `parsed` blindly.

task_description: Run two parallel chat requests for the same `thread_id` against the OpenAI Assistants API.
failure_reason: Threads do not support concurrent runs; the second request errors with `Thread already has an active run`.
error_message: Thread thread_XYZ already has an active run run_ABC.
what_was_tried: Letting two web requests interleave on the same thread.
lesson: Conversation state systems often serialize per-thread; design for it.
suggested_approach: Queue per-thread requests; create a new thread per concurrent task; or migrate to the Responses + Conversations APIs which have similar serialization semantics.

task_description: Bill internal customers based on token counts measured by `tiktoken` for a model served by Anthropic.
failure_reason: `tiktoken` is OpenAI-specific; counts diverge from Anthropic's tokenizer, so client invoices didn't match the provider's.
error_message: (billing reconciliation) — internal counts differ from provider counts.
what_was_tried: Using a single token counter across providers.
lesson: Tokenizers are model-family-specific; cross-provider counts are not interchangeable.
suggested_approach: Use `client.messages.count_tokens(...)` for Anthropic, `tiktoken.encoding_for_model(...)` for OpenAI, and provider-native tools for others.

task_description: Drop in `gpt-5` to replace `gpt-4o` and observe latency and bills doubling.
failure_reason: GPT-5 tends to produce more verbose outputs and (depending on configuration) uses reasoning tokens; without `max_completion_tokens` and prompt tuning, costs balloon.
error_message: (billing dashboard) — output token usage 2-3x baseline.
what_was_tried: Swapping the model string with no other changes.
lesson: Model swaps change cost/latency profiles even when API-compatible.
suggested_approach: A/B test on representative traffic; measure tokens per request; tune system prompts to enforce brevity; cap `max_completion_tokens`.

task_description: Move from Chat Completions to the Responses API and reuse the same `messages` array structure.
failure_reason: Responses uses a different `input` schema and stores state via `previous_response_id` or Conversations; reusing the messages contract leads to subtle errors.
error_message: (varies) — invalid_request_error: Unknown parameter, or state isn't carried as expected.
what_was_tried: Treating Responses as a renamed Chat Completions.
lesson: Responses introduces a new state model; conversation continuity is explicit.
suggested_approach: Read the Responses guide before migrating; use `previous_response_id` or `conversation` for state; rebuild any conversation history layer.

task_description: Build an MCP server that returns large file contents inline in tool results without checking client limits.
failure_reason: The MCP client's enclosing model exceeded its context window when the large blob was streamed back; the agent looped re-reading.
error_message: (no exception) — host model context truncated; agent retries reading.
what_was_tried: Returning entire file content as tool output.
lesson: MCP tool results enter the model's context; they need to be sized and chunked.
suggested_approach: Return references/summaries plus follow-up tools to fetch ranges; cap inline payloads; document size limits in tool descriptions.

task_description: Run an MCP server over stdio in a containerized environment without configuring stdin/stdout passthrough.
failure_reason: Container stdio handling buffered or detached the streams, so the MCP client saw the server hang at handshake.
error_message: (client log) — initialize request timed out; no response from server.
what_was_tried: Running the MCP server as a daemonized container.
lesson: stdio transports require unbuffered passthrough; containers commonly break this.
suggested_approach: Use unbuffered Python (`PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1`), run with `-i`/`-it`, or switch to MCP's HTTP/SSE transport.

task_description: Use `RecursiveCharacterTextSplitter` with default separators on Markdown documents.
failure_reason: Defaults split on whitespace/newlines that broke list items, code blocks, and tables in the middle, fragmenting structured content.
error_message: (no exception) — retrieved chunks contain orphaned list items or partial code.
what_was_tried: Defaults on a Markdown corpus.
lesson: Format-aware splitting matters; defaults assume prose.
suggested_approach: Use `MarkdownHeaderTextSplitter`, language-aware splitters for code, and table-aware extractors before chunking.

task_description: Average sentence embeddings to compute a paragraph embedding for retrieval.
failure_reason: Naive mean-pooling without normalization produced vectors with magnitudes that biased cosine similarity toward longer paragraphs.
error_message: (no exception) — top results consistently long; relevant short snippets buried.
what_was_tried: Mean-pooling without normalization.
lesson: Embedding aggregation is a modeling decision; defaults aren't always right.
suggested_approach: L2-normalize after pooling, weight by token count, or use a sentence-level embedding model designed for paragraphs.

task_description: Run a RAG eval where the same source documents appear in both the index and the test questions.
failure_reason: Eval leakage: the retrieval task became trivial because chunks were nearly verbatim copies of the queries.
error_message: (no exception) — recall@1 = 100%, but production performance is much lower.
what_was_tried: Generating eval questions from the same docs without holdout.
lesson: Realistic evals need holdout; otherwise metrics are uninformative.
