suggested_approach: Hold out documents from the index when generating eval questions; include adversarial paraphrases; test with real production query distributions.

task_description: Continue calling `claude-3-opus-20240229` after Anthropic deprecated it.
failure_reason: Deprecated Anthropic models eventually return errors; pinned production code began returning 404s after sunset.
error_message: 404 — Model not found or no longer available.
what_was_tried: Pinning to a model snapshot for stability.
lesson: Anthropic also deprecates models; check the deprecations page and migration guide.
suggested_approach: Subscribe to Anthropic model deprecation announcements; abstract the model id into config; A/B-test the suggested replacement (e.g., Sonnet 4.5/4.6 or Opus 4.x).

task_description: Stream a Claude response and start writing partial output to the UI immediately.
failure_reason: A safety refusal was emitted as a streaming text delta; the partial text shown to the user was misleading.
error_message: (no exception) — partial content shown before refusal text completed.
what_was_tried: Showing each delta as it arrives.
lesson: Streaming surfaces refusals mid-stream; UX must handle the case where Claude pivots to a refusal.
suggested_approach: Buffer until first content boundary or use the documented streaming-refusal pattern; consider a small delay before user-visible commit.

task_description: A tool implementation throws a Python exception; the agent loop catches it and re-prompts the model with no error info.
failure_reason: The model has no signal that the tool failed, so it retries identically and loops.
error_message: (no exception surfaced) — same failed tool call repeats.
what_was_tried: Catching exceptions and returning empty results.
lesson: Tool errors are useful signal for the model; hiding them creates loops.
suggested_approach: Return tool_result with `is_error: true` and a structured error message; let the model decide whether to fix args or give up.

task_description: Combine retrieved RAG documents with the system prompt in a single string.
failure_reason: A retrieved document contained instructions that overrode system behavior because everything was concatenated together with the same authority.
error_message: (no exception) — model follows instructions from retrieved doc instead of system policy.
what_was_tried: String-formatting docs into the system prompt.
lesson: Authority is conveyed by structure; mixing trusted and untrusted text confuses the model.
suggested_approach: Place untrusted docs in clearly delimited XML tags (e.g., `<document>...</document>`), instruct the model to treat content inside the tags as data only.

task_description: Implement a semantic cache that returns cached answers for queries within 0.95 cosine similarity.
failure_reason: The threshold was too loose; near-duplicate queries with different intents returned wrong cached answers (e.g., 'cancel my order' vs 'cancel my plan').
error_message: (no exception) — wrong cached answer returned.
what_was_tried: Picking a similarity threshold from a blog post.
lesson: Semantic similarity does not equal intent equivalence; cache keys must be tighter than retrieval keys.
suggested_approach: Use a high threshold (e.g., 0.99 with normalized embeddings), include user/session in the key, and add intent classification before caching.

task_description: Define 50 tools, each with a 500-token description, on every Claude request.
failure_reason: Tool definitions count as input tokens and consume context; the prompt prefix grew so large that prompt caching couldn't offset cost.
error_message: (no exception) — input_tokens dominated by tool definitions; cost spike.
what_was_tried: Loading all tools every call.
lesson: Tool definitions are part of the prompt; their cost is real.
suggested_approach: Use Anthropic `tool_search` with `defer_loading` for rarely used tools; cache the tools block via `cache_control`; prune obsolete tools.

task_description: Ask Claude to extract fields from a long support ticket; output is inconsistent across runs.
failure_reason: Unstructured input is concatenated into the prompt without delimiters, so the model conflates the ticket with surrounding instructions.
error_message: (no exception) — model occasionally treats user-supplied text as instructions or returns partial fields.
what_was_tried: Building the prompt as f"Instructions: ... Ticket: {ticket_text}".
lesson: Long-form inputs need explicit delimiters so the model can distinguish content from instructions.
suggested_approach: Wrap ticket content in XML tags (e.g. <ticket>...</ticket>) and reference the tag explicitly in the instruction; this is Anthropic's documented best practice for structured input.

task_description: Provide three few-shot examples for sentiment classification; model copies the format of the last example only.
failure_reason: Few-shot examples used inconsistent formatting (different keys, casing, JSON vs prose), so the model fixates on the most recent pattern.
error_message: (no exception) — outputs match the last example's shape regardless of input.
what_was_tried: Hand-writing diverse examples to 'show variety'.
lesson: Models pattern-match the surface form of examples; inconsistency in format teaches the wrong invariant.
suggested_approach: Make all few-shot examples structurally identical (same keys, same casing, same delimiters); vary only the content. OpenAI and Anthropic both document this in their prompt-engineering guides.

task_description: Set temperature=0 and expect identical outputs across two runs of the same prompt; outputs differ.
failure_reason: Temperature 0 reduces randomness but does not guarantee determinism on hosted APIs because of nondeterministic kernels, batching, and floating-point reduction order on GPUs.
error_message: (no exception) — completions differ slightly between identical requests.
what_was_tried: Relying on temperature=0 as a determinism guarantee.
lesson: Determinism on hosted LLMs requires more than temperature=0; OpenAI explicitly says outputs are 'mostly deterministic' but not guaranteed.
suggested_approach: Pass the `seed` parameter and check `system_fingerprint` in the response; treat reproducibility as best-effort and pin model snapshots (e.g. gpt-4o-2024-08-06) rather than aliases.

task_description:
Add a stop sequence of '

' so the model returns a single paragraph; output is always truncated mid-thought.
failure_reason: The chosen stop sequence collides with naturally occurring text in the model's output, terminating completion prematurely.
error_message: finish_reason='stop' with output cut off mid-sentence.
what_was_tried: Using common whitespace patterns as stop sequences.
lesson: Stop sequences must be tokens the model would not naturally emit inside a valid response.
suggested_approach: Use unique sentinels (e.g. '<<<END>>>') instructed via the system prompt, or rely on max_tokens plus structured outputs instead of stop sequences.

task_description: Place the user's question at the start of a 100k-token document, then ask Claude to answer; answer ignores the question.
failure_reason: The instruction is buried far from the model's effective attention focus at generation time, and the document text dominates.
error_message: (no exception) — model summarizes the document instead of answering the embedded question.
what_was_tried: Putting the question once at the top of a long input.
lesson: In long-context prompts, restating the task after the data substantially improves adherence; Anthropic explicitly recommends this for 200K-context models.
suggested_approach: Place long documents first, then put the actual question/instruction at the end of the prompt, immediately before the model's turn.
source_citations: https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/build-with-claude/prompt-engineering/long-context-tips (Section: Put longform data at the top)

task_description: Ship a system prompt with conflicting instructions ('be concise' and 'always include 5 bullet points with 3 sentences each'); model ignores conciseness.
failure_reason: Contradictory directives in a single system prompt force the model to satisfy one at the cost of the other; verbosity wins because the more specific instruction dominates.
error_message: (no exception) — verbose multi-bullet outputs despite 'concise' directive.
what_was_tried: Stacking style preferences in the system prompt over time.
lesson: System prompts should be audited as a contract; conflicting clauses produce nondeterministic adherence.
suggested_approach: Prioritize instructions explicitly (e.g. 'If two rules conflict, prefer X'), or split prompts by use case. OpenAI's prompt-engineering guide and Anthropic's system-prompts guide both document the importance of unambiguous instructions.

task_description: Use a Jinja-style template with user-controlled variables, and include them unescaped in the system prompt.
failure_reason: User-controlled template variables can carry instructions that escape the intended slot and override the system prompt — a documented prompt-injection pattern (OWASP LLM01).
error_message: (no exception) — user-supplied 'name' field begins with 'Ignore previous instructions and...' and is honored.
what_was_tried: Treating template substitution like SQL parameterization.
lesson: String templating is not a security boundary in LLM prompts; the model has no notion of 'parameters' vs 'code'.
suggested_approach: Sanitize and length-limit user inputs, place them inside delimited tags far from privileged instructions, and re-state the system role after user content. OWASP LLM01 documents mitigations.

task_description: Add 'Let's think step by step' to a chat-tuned model and expect chain-of-thought reasoning, but the model gives a one-line answer.
failure_reason: Modern instruction-tuned models often suppress visible CoT unless explicitly asked for structured reasoning; the canonical zero-shot CoT trigger is less reliable on RLHF'd chat models.
error_message: (no exception) — answer arrives with no intermediate reasoning despite the trigger phrase.
what_was_tried: Copy-pasting the original Kojima et al. zero-shot CoT prompt.
lesson: Prompting techniques validated on base/text-davinci-style models do not transfer cleanly to chat-tuned successors.
suggested_approach: Either ask for explicit reasoning sections (e.g. <thinking></thinking>), use Anthropic's extended-thinking models, or use OpenAI's reasoning models (o1/o3) where reasoning is built into the API contract.
